findings.passage: “Our democratic system of representative government depends on elections that are fair, honest and accurate,” said Victory, R-Hudsonville. “It is our responsibility to restore the public’s confidence in our elections by protecting everyone’s vote, making it harder to commit fraud and improving the system to ensure indisputable integrity.
findings.note: Statement in his name on a Senate package of election bills (SB 273-311, mostly about absentee ballot processes, audits and records), not on ID itself; quoted from the Senate caucus release.

findings.passage: We must make sure the good people of Michigan have their constitutional right to vote protected and have complete trust in the outcome.
findings.note: Same release; general statement on protecting the vote and trust in results.
SB 295, per the release, would require precinct workers to be trained in best practices for a balanced count, including checks on tabulators. Not an ID bill.
SB 306, per the release, would require the secretary of state to report on clerks not current with training and post it online. Not an ID bill.

findings.passage: There is strong bipartisan support among Michigan voters to have people verify their identity with an ID when voting. We must remain vigilant to protect the integrity of our elections, and this legislation will help to fix vulnerabilities in the system while also increasing access to IDs.
findings.note: From his Senate district newsletter (page shows no date) about Senate passage of bills to strengthen voting ID rules and ease getting a free state ID; the newsletter also describes SB 303 and a provisional-ballot route for voters without ID.
